source.title: WorkOS Releases auth.md: An Open Agent Registration Protocol Built on OAuth Standards
source.author: Asif Razzaq

athena.directive: Establish the Creative Liberation Engine as a pioneer in secure, auditable, and human-centric agent authentication by fully embracing and extending the `auth.md` protocol, ensuring both sovereign control and seamless interoperability for all AI agents.
athena.rationale: The `auth.md` protocol directly addresses the critical need for structured agent registration, auditing, and revocation, moving beyond insecure API key practices. By integrating and extending this open standard, the Creative Liberation Engine can solidify its position as a secure and compliant platform for advanced AI operations. This aligns with Article I: Sovereignty, by allowing us to control our authentication mechanisms, and Article IV: Quality Standards, by committing to a complete, robust solution rather than workarounds. It also ensures 'Zero human wait time' by automating agent registration processes.

options.title: Universal `auth.md` Interoperability Hub
options.description: Position the Creative Liberation Engine as a central hub for `auth.md` interactions, both consuming external `auth.md` services and publishing its own for internal/external agents. This establishes a robust, sovereign agent identity system.
options.tradeoffs: High initial complexity due to the dual-role implementation. Requires careful integration with existing Creative Liberation Engine Identity and Access Management (IAM) systems. The success of external consumption relies on broader industry adoption of `auth.md`.
options.architecture: Develop a core Agent Identity Service that acts as both an `auth.md` client and server. Implement both Agent Verified (ID-JAG) and User Claimed flows, including the necessary endpoints (`/agent/auth`, `claim_uri`, `revocation_uri`). Integrate with KEEPER for audit logging and RELAY for dynamic service discovery and routing of `auth.md` requests. Implement robust JWKS fetching and ID-JAG validation. For the User Claimed flow, integrate with SIGNAL for email-based OTP delivery.
options.design: A unified 'Agent Registry' dashboard. This dashboard would allow human users to: (1) view and manage all external services our agents are registered with (displaying granted permissions, facilitating selective revocation), and (2) configure and publish `auth.md` for Creative Liberation Engine services, defining scopes and flows via a guided wizard. Visual cues for real-time audit events and revocation status would be prominently displayed. The user experience for agent consent and OTP input would be streamlined and intuitive.

options.title: Creative Liberation Engine as a Sovereign `auth.md` Provider
options.description: Focus on publishing `auth.md` for all Creative Liberation Engine services, making our internal ecosystem agent-ready and auditable from day one, in line with Article I: Sovereignty.
options.tradeoffs: This approach does not immediately enable our agents to interact with *external* `auth.md` services. It requires significant internal adoption effort across all Creative Liberation Engine service teams to implement the `auth.md` endpoints and maintain their configuration.
options.architecture: Build an `auth.md` generation and hosting module that can be easily integrated into Creative Liberation Engine services, potentially as a sidecar or library. Implement the `/agent/auth`, `claim_uri`, and `revocation_uri` endpoints across our core services. Leverage our internal IAM for user matching and provisioning, and ensure robust handling of delegation records. Integrate audit event generation (e.g., `registration.created`, `claim.confirmed`) directly into KEEPER.
options.design: An 'Agent Service Configuration' interface allowing Creative Liberation Engine service owners to define their `auth.md` files, supported flows, and available scopes through a user-friendly GUI. A centralized 'Agent Activity Log' would visualize registration, claim, and revocation events with clear correlation to `agent_platform` and `(iss, sub)` for ID-JAG flows, enabling easy operator oversight and incident response.

options.title: Intelligent `auth.md` Client for External Agent Integration
options.description: Prioritize the ability of Creative Liberation Engine agents to discover and securely register with external services publishing `auth.md`, expanding our operational reach.
options.tradeoffs: This strategy does not address internal agent authentication standards for Creative Liberation Engine's own services. Its effectiveness is contingent on the broader adoption of `auth.md` by external services that our agents need to interact with.
options.architecture: Develop a sophisticated `auth.md` client library capable of robustly parsing `auth.md` files, navigating the discovery hops (401, PRM, Auth Server metadata), and executing both Agent Verified (ID-JAG request logic with external providers via SIGNAL) and User Claimed flows (handling OTP input). Implement secure storage and management of issued credentials for our agents.
options.design: An 'External Agent Connect' module within the Creative Liberation Engine. This would feature a discovery browser for `auth.md` services, a guided flow for agents to initiate registration, and a human-friendly interface for OTP input or consent confirmation. A visual representation of granted scopes and the ability for human users to easily revoke agent access to external services would be central to the design.

options.title: Advanced Agent Audit and Compliance Layer
options.description: Build a dedicated system within VERA and KEEPER to provide granular auditability and control over all agent registrations and activities, leveraging `auth.md`'s structured data for enhanced security and compliance.
options.tradeoffs: This option primarily focuses on observability and control, rather than on the initial `auth.md` registration mechanism itself. It requires `auth.md` to be implemented (either internally or by external services our agents interact with) to provide meaningful data.
options.architecture: Enhance KEEPER's memory schema to explicitly capture all `auth.md` audit events (e.g., `registration.created`, `claim.requested`, `otp.generated`, `claim.confirmed`, `registration.expired`, `registration.revoked`), including critical metadata like `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, and `agent_platform`. Develop VERA validation rules for agent access and activity patterns. Implement a robust, centralized revocation API that can trigger provider-side logout tokens or revoke internal delegation records.
options.design: A 'Compliance & Audit Dashboard' providing real-time, filterable visibility into all agent activities by service, agent, and event type. This would include interactive graphs visualizing agent access patterns and potential anomalies. A 'Revocation Control Panel' would allow human operators to selectively revoke agent access based on delegation records, with clear confirmation flows and an audit trail of revocation actions.

options.title: Agent-First Developer Experience (DX) with `auth.md`
options.description: Transform the Creative Liberation Engine's developer experience to treat AI agents as first-class citizens, with `auth.md` as the foundational protocol for secure interaction and streamlined development.
options.tradeoffs: This is more of an enablement layer than a core architectural component itself. Its success and impact are highly dependent on the underlying `auth.md` implementation being robust and complete. It requires ongoing maintenance to keep documentation and tooling up-to-date with protocol evolution.
options.architecture: Integrate `auth.md` protocol specifications directly into our API Gateway and SDK generation processes. Develop comprehensive documentation, tutorials, and code samples specifically for agents interacting via `auth.md`. Automate `auth.md` file generation from API definitions and service metadata, ensuring consistency and accuracy. Provide sandbox environments for developers to test agent registration flows.
options.design: A dedicated 'Agent Developer Portal' within the Creative Liberation Engine's documentation, featuring interactive `auth.md` explorers, sandbox environments for agent registration, and clear guides for integrating with Creative Liberation Engine services as an agent. Visualizations of API scopes and how they map to `auth.md` definitions would enhance clarity. The user interface for granting consent for agent actions would be streamlined and clearly communicate permissions.
